page.layout: One text column of running text, with no marginal notes and no footnotes. Running head at the top, page number at the upper left, catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: permittit evenire, quæ à Revelato Dei Verbo ( solâ Bonæ Conscientiæ & Actionum clara, statâ, tutâ Regula ) multum abest ut comprobentur.

Atque adeo confido, Caufæ meæ Justitiâ & Conscientiæ Rectitudine Me tanto Illis futurum in Foro Dei superiorem, quanto Illos supra Me extulit Fortuna in illo Vulgi judicio; qui non cogitat plurima sæpe hominum facinora ad Cælos usque attolli plausu mundi, qui si ex injustitia & scelerato fine censeantur, ex Inferno ascendunt: Quin nec Aura illa secunda quæ Piratæ velum implet, statim ipsius latrocinia & rapinas excusat.

Multo interim libentius & alacrius fero perdidisse hanc litem (quam coactus admodum sufcepi, ad affercendas Leges Regni, Libertatem & Honorem Parlamentarium, Jura Coronæ, justas Subditorum Immunitates, & veram Religionem Christianam in Doctrina, Disciplina, cæterisque incitamentis & præmiis debitis) quàm si multo Bello potiori ad hæc omnia opprimenda valuissem; id quod nonnulli jam palam faciunt, quicquid priùs simulaverant.

Plurimum interim mihi proderit Patientia amicorum & Preces ad mitigandam hujus poculi amaritudinem, quam ut à Dei manu (si fic fieri necesse fit) libentius accipiô & haurio, quàm ab illis porrigitur eâ sæva & impia manu contra Me toties levatâ.
In his autem extremis, plus Hostibus videor quàm Amicis debere: illi finem imponent

page.notes: Running head is set in Greek capitals; the printed Greek is read as ΕΙΚΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΚΗ, with the third-from-last letter group possibly Λ printed in a form close to A. Catchword "ærumnosæ" stands alone at the right below the last line and is the first word of the next page. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. Several words are set in a different face (italic) and are marked accordingly where the type is clearly distinct; the exact extent of italics in the lines around "Me", "Illis" and "Cælos" is judged from the scan.
